text:
Elaine Walker: Quick kickoff idea — "snackloop" tutorial series: 3 short dev tutorials (~7min each) + a sample repo + an explainer blog. Target: engineers who want a working Redwood demo in a day. Clear CTA: $100 credits + gated webinar.

Marco Chen: Nice. Suggest pairing each tutorial with a tiny benchmark narrative: 1) latency for local dev, 2) cost/batching for throughput, 3) private deploy checklist. One chart + one takeaway per tutorial.

Priya Nair: Distribution: carousel social posts, a long-form blog, and a gated webinar/workshop that demos the sample app. Webinar funnels to SDRs.

Samir Patel: On funnel: gated webinar signups should include utm_campaign=snackloop, source=snackable-tutorials, and a short form field for "expected tokens per call" so we can route high-usage leads to AE.

Dana Ortiz: Copy angle: "Ship an LLM feature in a day — predictable latency, lower cost." Keep it dev-forward. Include code snippet in the blog showing the API call.

Elaine Walker: Social copy draft: `Try our 1-day prototype: 3 bite-sized tutorials + sample app. Get $100 credits to deploy on Redwood. Sign up -> link` — we should A/B vs "Prototype LLM features in hours."

Marco Chen: I'll include a tiny bench script in the repo, e.g.:```bash
# simple latency run
python tools/bench_latency.py --model redwood-3b --seq 128 --n 50
```

Priya Nair: Timeline owners: I can do the blog + webinar outline. Samir, can you own the form and HubSpot routing? Marco, sample app + bench script. Dana, social assets and short videos? Elaine will coordinate release cadence.

Samir Patel: For routing I'll add form fields: utm_campaign, source_tier, expected_tokens_per_call and wire them into HubSpot. Also add an optional checkbox: "Request Dedicated demo" to flag enterprise intent.

Dana Ortiz: Visuals: 3 x 15s clips (one per tutorial) + a 60s overview. I'll do storyboards in Figma by Fri EOD. Need the bench chart (png + csv) from Marco to animate.

Marco Chen: Repo structure proposal: `/tutorials/snackloop/01-latency`, `/02-cost`, `/03-private` with minimal READMEs and a docker-compose for local dev. I'll add bench_output/latency_chart.png and bench_output/latency.csv tomorrow.

Elaine Walker: KPIs: blog pageviews, tutorial video completions (target 50% watch), webinar signups, signups->paid conversions (30d), and lead score distribution. We'll set baseline after week 1.

Priya Nair: Webinar format: 35m demo + 15m QA. Follow-up email includes 2 deep-dive links for ops (batching, quantization).

Samir Patel: PublishingBot: please create launch event and a draft landing page.

PublishingBot: Event created: "Snackloop tutorial launch" on 2026-05-14 10:00 PDT — landing page placeholder: https://redwood.example/landing/snackloop (status: draft).

Dana Ortiz: Small ask: can Marco export a clean PNG + raw CSV for the latency chart so I can animate?

Marco Chen: Yup. I'll push bench_output/latency_chart.png and bench_output/latency.csv by AM. Default examples will use sequence_length=128 to match the bench.

Elaine Walker: Action items + due dates: Priya (blog + webinar outline) Tue, Marco (sample app + bench scripts) Wed AM, Dana (social + storyboards) Fri EOD, Samir (form + routing) Wed EOD. I'll assign tasks in Asana and announce in #general on launch day. :rocket: 

Samir Patel: :thumbsup: 

Priya Nair: Also proposing a small prompt-eval harness in the repo to show before/after quality when using quantization/batching — helps preempt quality concerns.

Samir Patel: Add UTM to sample app README links so demos preserve tracking: `?utm_source=repo&utm_campaign=snackloop`

Elaine Walker: Check legal/security on live data usage in examples. If needed, well use generated datasets. Dana/Priya to confirm.

Dana Ortiz: I'll confirm with security today. If scrubbing is required, we'll mock data.

Marco Chen: One tech note: recommend default `sequence_length=128` in examples to keep latency/cost claims consistent.

Elaine Walker: Great. If no blockers we proceed. I'll post kickoff doc and do the final checklist. Thanks team! :rocket:
